gen_risks.description: Insufficient capacity to develop and operate the state EMIS and digital assessment tools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated EMIS team, embed IPF‑TA technical experts, set phased milestones and monitor progress through the PMC.
gen_risks.evidence: State EMIS will be developed under IPF‑TA component; capacity building needed for nodal institutions (Section 41).

gen_risks.description: Lack of a standardized student assessment system and limited SAC capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen SCERT Assessment Cell, launch periodic SLAS, train staff on item‑level data collection, and integrate results with EMIS.
gen_risks.evidence: State lacks periodic SLAS and SAC does not collect student/item‑level data (Section 13).

gen_risks.description: Delay in establishing a structured in‑service TaRL teacher training programme.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fast‑track TaRL curriculum design, allocate blended‑learning resources, monitor trainer deployment, and set clear completion checkpoints.
gen_risks.evidence: Baseline states system lacks a structured long‑term in‑service teacher training program on TaRL (DLI 4).

gen_risks.description: Absence of an annual procurement plan may cause procurement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Draft and approve an annual procurement plan per the FMP manual, assign a procurement specialist, and track against the schedule.
gen_risks.evidence: Assessment found no practice of preparing an annual procurement plan (Section 4.5).

gen_risks.description: Substantial fiduciary risk due to systemic gaps in financial management.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement IFSA recommendations, augment FM staff, conduct regular internal audits, and enforce strict control procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Fiduciary risk of the Program is assessed as ‘Substantial’ (Section 56).

gen_risks.description: Budget execution delays caused by multi‑tier planning and limited capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Streamline AWP&B approval (target ≤3 months), provide budgeting capacity‑building, and use interim financing where needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Multiple tiers of planning and limited capacity lead to inadequately planned budgeting and fund release delays (Section 59).

gen_risks.description: Construction of model composite schools delayed by droughts or floods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate disaster‑resilient designs, schedule works in favorable seasons, and maintain buffer time in the project timeline.
gen_risks.evidence: State vulnerable to droughts and floods which can extend school breaks and affect construction timelines (Section 3).

gen_risks.description: Disbursement delays if DLI verification and data collection are not completed on time.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen verification team, use digital data submission, and schedule verification activities early in each fiscal year.
gen_risks.evidence: DLIs require field‑based verification and data collection, which may delay disbursements (DLIs verification protocols).

gen_risks.description: Teacher shortage and high pupil‑teacher ratios limit training effectiveness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate recruitment, use contract teachers, provide incentives for subject specialists, and deliver remote training modules.
gen_risks.evidence: Majority of teachers lack adequate training; many teach 2‑3 grades, indicating shortage (Section 11).

gen_risks.description: Community resistance to boys’ residential schools and dropout norms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run community‑engagement campaigns, develop residential facilities for boys, and offer scholarships/incentives to keep boys in school.
gen_risks.evidence: Families prefer boys to work; residential schools for boys not currently available (Section 6).

gen_risks.description: Weak grievance redress mechanism may erode community trust.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade GRM to an online portal, set SLA for response times, train staff, and publish regular grievance reports.
gen_risks.evidence: Need for strengthening grievance redress mechanism for escalation and monitoring (Section 67).

gen_risks.description: New personal‑data protection legislation could affect data handling procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct legal impact analysis, update data‑handling SOPs, train staff on compliance, and embed safeguards in contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: New personal data protection legislation may impact activities; technical analysis required (Legal covenants Section III.C).

gen_risks.description: Construction activities may generate waste, pollution, and lack fire‑safety compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt an environmental management plan, enforce waste segregation, include fire‑safety standards in designs, and train contractors.
gen_risks.evidence: Construction may cause uncontrolled waste, pollution, and lacks fire safety norms (Section 70).

gen_risks.description: Increasing climate‑change impacts (heatwaves, heavy precipitation) threaten school operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct climate‑risk screening, incorporate green building features, and develop school emergency response plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change will increase erratic temperatures and heavy precipitation, threatening school operations (Section 72).

gen_risks.description: SIS‑SS staffed at only ~70 % of sanctioned strength, limiting implementation capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit to fill vacancies, offer retention incentives, and cross‑train existing staff to cover critical functions.
gen_risks.evidence: SIS‑SS operates at approximately 70 % of sanctioned staff strength (Section 14).

gen_risks.description: Weak internal audit and control mechanisms may lead to compliance gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated internal‑audit unit, adopt a risk‑based audit plan, and ensure timely follow‑up on audit observations.
gen_risks.evidence: Deviations observed in control implementation; lack of focused internal audit system (Section 15).

gen_risks.description: Reliance on under‑funded technical support agencies could limit capacity‑building outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure multi‑year funding agreements with agencies, build in‑house capacity, and monitor deliverables against milestones.
gen_risks.evidence: Technical support agencies are underfunded and may not sustain interventions (Section 4.4).

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is rated Substantial. State elections are due in December 2023 and the associated large democratic exercise could slow down activities envisioned for the first year of the operation. The window between the operation being declared effective and the state elections is small.
gt_risks.mitigation: Disruptions are expected to be minimal given that the state intends to initiate work and complete necessary field work and/or data collection well before the elections, and utilize the election period for analysis and training module/materials development. The implementing bodies (SIS-SS, SCERT, SIEMAT, and SAC) will need to move swiftly to realize the state's plans.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design of operation risk is rated Substantial. Certain context-specific attributes such as topography and underlying community representation in overall enrolment could raise challenges, including barriers to school enrolment such as lack of physical access in sparsely populated areas with poor road connectivity, or high opportunity cost of schooling due to informal-sector employment.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Government of Chhattisgarh has addressed similar challenges in the past through development and rollout of customized solutions; the project will enable planning for residential facilities for students and teachers in model schools in topographically hard-to-reach areas.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk is rated Substantial. In some cases, nodal educational institutions lack the expertise to implement technically complex interventions.
gt_risks.mitigation: Onboarding a Program Management Consultant (PMC) and technical support agencies is expected to significantly reduce the risks involved. Sustainability post-completion will be ensured through careful planning, technical support for capacity building of nodal institutions, and institutionalizing new mechanisms.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk is rated Substantial. Considering the implementing arrangements and diverse capacity across implementing agencies, implementation constraints can be foreseen in public financial management arrangements and compliance with rules and regulations for accountability.
gt_risks.mitigation: Focused attention in the short/medium term on enhanced effectiveness of planning, budgeting, and fund flow processes; adequacy of staffing and capacity building of fiduciary staff; strengthened monitoring through internal and external independent reviews; timely resolution of independent external review observations; a robust dedicated procurement complaints redressal system; strengthened contract management for delivery of goods and works; and ensuring exclusion of Bank-debarred firms from high-value contracts.
